items.excerpt: Manchester United's Michael Carrick hailed the second performance of his team after they came back from two goals down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.

items.title: Fernandes claims players don't need to save Carrick's job, but did they?
items.excerpt: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has come out in support of head coach Michael Carrick, but reiterated that the players didn't need to save his job in their 3-2 comeback win against Roma.
body: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has come out in support of head coach Michael Carrick, but reiterated that the players didn't need to save his job in their 3-2 comeback win against Roma.
United and Carrick looked dead and buried within the first 18 minutes as the Italian side took a two-goal lead in the early exchanges.

It prompted boos and protests from supporters, who threw tennis balls onto the pitch, but the Red Devils turned things around as a Fernandes penalty and a late Matheus Cunha double gave them their first win in 54 days.
The spirit shown in the performance suggested at least some on-pitch support for Carrick, whose tenure appeared to have been hanging on by a thread ever since the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth .

items.title: Cunha completes wild Man Utd comeback win over Roma from two down
items.excerpt: Manchester United produced an extraordinary comeback from two down to beat Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford and pick up their first win in 10 games.
body: Manchester United produced an extraordinary comeback from two down to beat Roma 3-2 at Old Trafford and pick up their first win in 10 games.

Michael Carrick looked on the brink when his disjointed team were completely undone for Matias Soule's opener and Donyell Malen soon made it two from the penalty spot. But Matheus Cunha won one of his own, scored two and was sent off in a wild contest.

United had been booed off at the break and when Carlos Baleba had to go off early in the second half with a hamstring injury it all looked dismal for United. But when Cunha won a penalty that Bruno Fernandes scored after a retake it altered the momentum. As it happened | Teams | Stats | Latest: Man Utd Not got Sky? Bryan Mbeumo struck both posts with one shot soon after and the noise inside Old Trafford was astonishing thereafter. Roma cleared one off the line and United had two more penalty shouts as the Italian side - unbeaten in Serie A - began to wobble badly.

items.title: Raphinha double sees Barca power past Villa
items.excerpt: Raphinha's second-half double inspired Barcelona to a 3-0 victory against Aston Villa at the Camp Nou as Unai Emery's side saw their three-game winning run in the Champions League come to an end.
body: Raphinha's second-half double inspired Barcelona to a 3-0 victory against Aston Villa at the Camp Nou as Unai Emery's side saw their three-game winning run in the Champions League come to an end.

Villa boss Emery returned to his homeland on his 55th birthday and with his team in great form having lost just one of their previous nine encounters, only to come crashing down in the driving Catalan rain.

The home side have been in free-scoring form this season, averaging four goals a game and they got on the scoresheet within seven minutes. Joao Gomes laid the ball on a plate to, of all people, Lamine Yamal, for the Spain forward's 13th goal of this campaign. He also has 11 assists to his name. items.excerpt: Sam Dalby's sixth goal of the season earned Bolton a 1-0 victory at misfiring Charlton.
body: Sam Dalby's sixth goal of the season earned Bolton a 1-0 victory at misfiring Charlton.
The result piles more pressure on Addicks boss Nathan Jones with the south-east Londoners now winless in 11 matches, and a fourth straight Championship loss dropped them to 21st in the table.
Bolton captain Josh Sheehan pulled the midfield strings during the opening 45 minutes and produced a whipped shot wide after five minutes.

Charlton had the first of the minimal openings in the first half on seven minutes. Tyreece Campbell's deep cross picked out Danny McNamara's run to the far post but the right-sided wing-back's attempt to convert was frustrated by Wanderers goalkeeper Jack Bonham.

items.title: Birmingham cruise past Millwall
items.excerpt: Alex Cochrane scored inside a minute as Birmingham buried Millwall with a first-half goal rush to earn a 3-0 win in the Championship at St. Andrew's.
body: Alex Cochrane scored inside a minute as Birmingham buried Millwall with a first-half goal rush to earn a 3-0 win in the Championship at St. Andrew's.
Cochrane, Max Bird and Jay Stansfield netted with left-footed finishes before half-time to ease the loss of seven-goal striker August Priske with a knee problem.
It put City on their way to their sixth win in eight and extended their unbeaten Championship home start to seven games.

Cochrane netted when he lashed home a loose ball from 30 yards when Millwall failed to clear a long pass and Phil Neumann's shot hit a defender. Goalkeeper Max Crocombe was motionless on his line as Cochrane netted for the second successive game.

items.title: Norwich thrash Derby to heap pressure on Eustace
items.excerpt: Norwich piled more pressure on Derby boss John Eustace after thrashing the Championship strugglers 4-0 at Pride Park.
body: Norwich piled more pressure on Derby boss John Eustace after thrashing the Championship strugglers 4-0 at Pride Park.
On his 47th birthday, Eustace saw his side ripped apart by the pace and movement of the Canaries, who scored three times before the break.

Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma and Darlin Yongwa put Norwich in complete control before substitute Jovon Makama wrapped up a third straight win for the visitors and condemned Derby to a fourth defeat in five games.
Derby have won only once this season and Friday night's home game with Bolton now looks like a huge one for Eustace.
